title: Many still unsure about retirement target
full_text:
Nearly two-thirds of Australians have not landed on a figure for their retirement nest egg, while around half of those aged 55 and over are still yet to set a savings target, according to new research from Selfwealth by Syfe.
“The Lifetime of Investing” report, based on a study by YouGov using a survey in September and early October of 1060 people aged over 18, found approaches to building wealth varied according to age and circumstances, but gaps in planning, financial knowledge and investment confidence meant many had no clear path toward their goals.
The report found 61 per cent of Australians had not calculated how much they will need for retirement, 40 per cent had yet to work out a savings target, 21 per cent had chosen a figure that “feels right” and around 10 per cent to 15 per cent had used a calculator or sought advice.
Selfwealth found where a calculator or adviser had been used to set a target, 52 per cent of respondents were more confident they would meet it compared with 15 per cent to 20 per cent of those who have not calculated a number.
Of concern was the finding that 47 per cent of those aged 55 and over have not calculated a retirement savings target, compared with 29 per cent of those aged 18-24, and when asked if they would like to invest more money, over 60 per cent agreed that was the case, but 53 per cent said not having enough money at present was a barrier to investing.
Selfwealth acting head of Australia and Syfe chief operating officer Samantha Horton said the findings show a gap between what people would like to achieve and the actions they are taking.
“Australians have a lot competing for their money and, for many people, super feels like the retirement plan that’s already taken care of. That’s completely understandable,” Horton said.
“But for many, super alone may not fund the retirement they’re picturing, especially if they’d like to stop work earlier or as living costs rise and people live longer.
“Working out how much you’ll need is a simple first step and the earlier people do it, the more options they have to build towards it at their own pace.”
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation and Investments
